claims.statement: Admission (`nora.engagement.stages.admission.run`) is a pure, non-awaiting decision function returning one of four verdicts (RUN_NOW, QUEUED, QUEUE_FULL, REJECTED); it acquires the conversation's slot only on RUN_NOW, and a QUEUED verdict deliberately does not acquire because the lock already belongs to the in-flight turn.

The pipeline calls `admission.run` outside the try/finally that owns the conversation key and opens the releasing block only for an admitted tag, so a rejected tag never releases a key that, in the in-flight case, belongs to a different still-running tag.

`ConversationSlots.release_and_dispatch` performs the release and the dequeue/re-acquire/spawn of the next waiting tag as a single synchronous call with no await in the gap, so no arriving tag can slip into the RUN_NOW path and a release that skipped dispatch cannot strand the queue.

The per-conversation FIFO queue is bounded and self-draining: admission sheds the newest tag and counts `nora_tags_dropped_total{reason="queue_full"}` when depth is already at maxlen, there is deliberately no staleness rule, and a drained conversation retains nothing.

A queued turn's context is assembled at dequeue time rather than at arrival, so tag 2 sees tag 1's reply already in the transcript; the queue feeds the single in-flight slot in order instead of widening it.

Enqueuing a tag carries a zero-argument factory plus the trace context captured at admission, and identity is not stored in the queue but re-resolved (memoized, in-process) at dequeue, so the slots object holds no reference back into the pipeline.
The progress reaction is fired at admission for both RUN_NOW and QUEUED tags and never for a REJECTED or QUEUE_FULL tag, and it is spawned rather than awaited so it adds no latency to the turn.

Inside the turn body the order is fixed: bind the tag id for logging, assemble the TagContext, rehydrate @-mention placeholders from `raw_json`, select tag doctrine, read the conversation's policy entry, build the DeliveryHandle, construct the per-tag Room, build the tool surface, then build the prefill and the tag message.

The room's MCP allowlist is computed once before `deliver.build` and reused as the guard's `budgets=` input, because `ToolRegistry.budgets()` only folds an MCP tool's budget in when its server is in that set; a guard built from a different set could disclose a tool name the conversation cannot call.

`invoke.run` makes exactly one bounded attempt: `asyncio.wait_for` enforces the tier timeout while `turn_deadline` publishes the same number to tools; a timeout and a generic exception return `ok=False` silently and are counted, while a `PartialReplyError` returns `ok=False` with `stop_reason="max_tokens"` and the partial text so the caller may salvage it.

`invoke.run` threads the loop's stop reason back to the pipeline because `ok` alone cannot distinguish a model that declined to speak from a loop Strands terminated on a cap, and `deliver.check_outcome` needs that value to label the silent turn.

The reply leaves as a tool call because `tool_choice="required"` applies to the turn's first model call and is relaxed to `auto` only once a terminal verb has run, while `ReplyGuard._before_model` cancels further model calls after the terminal budget is spent — which is why nothing in her own loop runs after the reply and the post-turn fold needs a second model.

`Deliverer` is the only caller of `adapter.send` and is constructed only in `deliver.build`, whose callers are pinned to the named sending paths on the AST, because every send guard (R-2 latch, R-4, R-6, R-18, audit-first write) lives inside `Deliverer.deliver`.

The sender latches attempts rather than successes, and its `message_cap` is the same number as the guard's `send_reply` budget, threaded from one `budgets["send_reply"]` mapping so the refusal cannot be reported under the wrong rule.

Delivery is audit-first: a PENDING row is appended before `adapter.send`, the row's outcome is written afterwards with the platform's timestamp, and an audit-append failure refuses the send and counts `audit_write_failed`.

`deliver.check_outcome` decides the silent-turn label from state the sender already holds: with `called` false it counts `no_send_call` unless the stop reason names an R-8 cap, and with `called` true it adds no increment because the guard refusal was already counted by name.

Three recovery nets — salvage, the cut-off fallback (drafted text, else the canned line) and DEC-93's recovery — share one gate, `_nothing_answered`, which is also true when a landed heads-up still owes its answer, and all three are occasion-gated off for a participation request.

Only the canned `_EXHAUSTED_FALLBACK` line departs from the rule that she sends only what `send_reply` sent; drafted, salvaged and recovered deliveries are her own words and flow through the same `deliver` path as a normal reply, so the guards, Markdown conversion, link carry and audit row all still apply.

A successful salvage deliberately does not return early: the turn flows on to `check_outcome`, which reads `deliverer.delivered` as True and gives it the same trace correction, Honcho feed and completion accounting as a normal delivery, while a refused salvage returns silently.

The turn's disposition is derived once from `delivered`, `called` and the recovery flag, written to the shared decision log as one of three verdicts (replied, silent, failed) before the not-delivered return, and surfaced on both the turn span and `nora_engagement_outcomes_total` through a single label function.

A crashed turn clears its trace so retention never persists a placeholder outcome as if the turn had succeeded, while the decision log still records the fault with verdict `failed` and reason `handler_error`.

The debrief runs in the turn's `finally`, with the disposition already final and before `release_and_dispatch`, so it holds the conversation slot, reviews silent/vetoed/timed-out turns as well as delivered ones, and is gated both on wiring and on an attributable trace.

The raw TagTrace is retained by spawning the save (never awaiting it) and counting `nora_tagtrace_writes_total{outcome}` beside the spawn, and it is not gated the way the Honcho feedback feed is, because a silent, vetoed or timed-out turn still produces reasoning worth retaining.

One tagged message produces one trace: the entry point opens a `generation` root before admission so a rejected tag leaves a trace that says it was rejected, and a queued turn re-attaches the context captured at its own admission instead of inheriting the dispatching task's context, which would file it under the previous person's tag.

The span layer must not raise at this call site: `release_and_dispatch` runs in a `finally` past the outer handler, so an exception from a span or context attach would skip the lock release and wedge the conversation with no error anywhere.

The outer handler is `except BaseException`, not `except Exception`, so a fault that is not an Exception (such as `asyncio.CancelledError`) is absorbed instead of crashing the spawning task and `nora_silent_failures_total{reason="handler_error", audience="tag"}` is still incremented, while `finally` releases the slot either way.

A partially delivered turn is its own observable: `deliver.truncation_reason` combines `stop_reason` and the `completed` flag, and the turn's `finally` counts `nora_partial_replies_total{reason}` whenever at least one message had already gone out.

Platform resolution fails closed in two opposite directions on purpose: an unknown platform raises rather than falling back to another adapter, because delivering to the wrong room is worse than failing loudly, while a missing roster source degrades to UNAVAILABLE rather than reporting an empty room.
